text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin assessing the newborn's jaundice, when was the baby born, and at what age in hours did the yellowish discoloration first appear?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Total and Direct Bilirubin Levels, CBC with Reticulocyte Count, Direct Coombs Test, Blood Type and Rh of Mother and Infant.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Total Bilirubin: 7 mg/dL, Direct Bilirubin: 0.6 mg/dL, Hemoglobin: 17.6 g/dL, Reticulocytes: 0.3%, Maternal Blood Group: A, Rh-negative, Fetal Blood Group: 0, Rh-positive

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show a normal bilirubin level for a 5-day-old and no signs of hemolysis or blood group incompatibility, which strongly suggests physiologic jaundice. Since the baby is feeding well and the bilirubin is within expected limits, I am confident in my assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiologic Jaundice
